  - text: CLASS 9 · REAL NUMBERS
  - heading "Terminating and Non-Terminating Decimals" [level=1]
  - paragraph: "Objective: Predict whether a rational number terminates from its simplified denominator."
  - text: 18 min INTERMEDIATE CONCEPT number
  - link "School lessons":
    - /url: /lessons/school

    - text: School lessons

  - main:
    - heading "▣ FACTOR-DENOMINATOR MACHINE" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Simplify → Factor denominator → Predict → Verify
    - article:
      - heading "1 Enter a fraction" [level=3]
      - spinbutton "Numerator": "7"
      - spinbutton "Denominator": "40"
      - button "Swap numerator and denominator":
        - img
      - button "Reset fraction":
        - img
    - text: →
    - article:
      - heading "2 Cancel common factors" [level=3]
      - text: 7 40 = 7÷1 40÷1 = 7 40
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Already in lowest terms.
    - text: →
    - article:
      - heading "3 Factor the denominator" [level=3]
      - paragraph: 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5
      - strong: = 2³ × 5
      - text: 2 2 2 5
      - complementary:
        - text: Other prime factors
        - emphasis: "3"
        - emphasis: "7"
        - emphasis: "11"
        - emphasis: ...
    - article:
      - heading "4 Prediction" [level=3]
      - strong: TERMINATES
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: The denominator in lowest terms is 2ᵐ5ⁿ.
      - text: "Rule: In lowest terms, p/q terminates iff q = 2ᵐ5ⁿ, otherwise it recurs."
      - complementary: ⚠ Testing the unsimplified denominator can give the wrong prediction.
    - article:
      - heading "5 Verify decimal" [level=3]
      - strong: 7 40 = 0.175
      - text: Terminating Tenths 1 Hundredths 7 Thousandths 5
      - emphasis: 0 0 ...
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: Terminates after 3 decimal places.
    - img
    - text: "Rule in words: A rational number p/q (in lowest terms) has a terminating decimal expansion if and only if the denominator q has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Equivalently: q = 2ᵐ5ⁿ"
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Powers of 2 give factors of 10 like 2 × 5; together 2ᵐ5ⁿ creates 10ᵏ.
      - paragraph: So q = 2ᵐ5ⁿ ⇒ p/q can be written over an integer power of 10, which terminates.
      - paragraph: If q has any other prime factor, it cannot be absorbed into 10ᵏ, so the decimal repeats.
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLES" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "Example 1: 7/40 terminates"
      - paragraph: 40 = 2³ × 5¹ → only 2 and 5 → terminates.
      - paragraph:
        - text: 7/40 = 0.175
        - emphasis: Terminates
      - paragraph: "Example 2: 7/12 recurs"
      - paragraph: 12 = 2² × 3 → includes 3 → recurs.
      - paragraph: 7/12 = 0.583333...
    - article:
      - heading "⚠ COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]
      - text: If you test the unsimplified denominator, you may get the wrong answer.
      - paragraph: "Example: 18/75"
      - paragraph: 75 = 3 × 5² (has 3) → you may think it recurs.
      - paragraph: But 18/75 = 6/25, and 25 = 5² → it terminates.
    - heading "⚑ MINI CHALLENGE" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Challenge: Simplify 18/75, factor the denominator and predict its decimal type."
    - article:
      - heading "1 Simplify" [level=3]
      - paragraph: 18 75 = 18÷3 75÷3 = 6 25
      - text: "Lowest terms: 6/25"
      - img
    - text: →
    - article:
      - heading "2 Factor denominator" [level=3]
      - paragraph: 25 = 5 × 5 = 5²
      - text: "5 5 Only prime factor: 5"
    - text: →
    - article:
      - heading "3 Predict" [level=3]
      - strong: TERMINATES
      - paragraph: 25 = 5² = 2⁰5²
      - img
    - text: →
    - article:
      - heading "4 Verify" [level=3]
      - paragraph: 18 75 = 6 25 = 0.24
      - text: Terminates after 2 decimal places.
      - img
    - text: "Answer: 18/75 = 0.24 (terminating)"
    - img
